summary_en: A 'cognitive process' (vīthi, literally 'street' or 'path') is the orderly, gapless series of mind-moments that arises when an object is taken up through one of the six doors. Margaya stresses that nothing a person does happens in a single mind-moment: seeing properly, hearing, speaking, understanding someone's words, moving a limb, walking, giving and taking each require a whole series. It adds that the mind is extremely hard to know, because it is invisible, intangible and too fast to test, and it is the very tool doing the knowing. Even students therefore know these processes only by inference. Pradeepika sets out six 'sixes' needed to locate any mind in a process (bases, doors, objects, kinds of consciousness, processes, and intensities of the object) and divides processes into five-door and mind-door processes.

sinhala_explanation.heading: 'වීථි' යන වචනය සහ චිත්ත වීථියේ අර්ථය
sinhala_explanation.text: ලෝක ව්‍යවහාරයේ මිනිසුන් ගමන් කරන මාර්ගයට 'වීථි' යයි කියයි; සිත් පවතින ක්‍රමයද එවැනි මාර්ගයක් බැවින් වීථි නම් වේ [C038-P:L29]. තවද ආවර්ජනාදි අනේක සිත් පිළිවෙළින් එකිනෙක ගැටීම, සදොරෙහි නොයෙක් සිත් පිළිවෙළ හටගැනීම, චිත්ත සන්තානය පැවතීම යන අර්ථවලින්ද වීථි නම් වේ [C038-P:L29]. එබැවින් සදොරින් එක් දොරකින් ගත් අරමුණක් එල්බගෙන අතරක් නැතිව පිළිවෙළින් උපදින සිත් පෙළ 'චිත්ත වීථිය' යි [C038-P:L29]. මාර්ගය එය 'ඒ ඒ කරුණු සිදු කිරීම් වශයෙන් ඇති වන චිත්ත පරම්පරා, සිත් වැල්' ලෙස හඳුන්වයි; කෙටියෙන් කිවහොත් එක් එක් කරුණක් සම්බන්ධයෙන් ඇති වන සිත් වැලයි [C038-M:L3].

sinhala_explanation.heading: එක් සිතකින් කිසිවක් සිදු නොවේ (මාර්ගය)
sinhala_explanation.text: ඇසට හමුවන දෙය හරියට දැනගැනීම, කනට එන ශබ්ද, නාසයට, දිවට, කයට පැමිණෙන ගන්ධ, රස, ස්පර්ශ හරියට දැනගැනීම, වචනයක් කීම, අනුන් කියන වචනයේ තේරුම දැනගැනීම, ශරීරාවයව එසවීම, පහත් කිරීම, එහා මෙහා කිරීම, යෑම, ඊම, දීම, ගැනීම යන කිසිවක් එක් සිතකින් සිදු නොවේ; එක් එක් කරුණක් සඳහා ක්‍රමානුකූලව සිත් පෙළක් ඇති විය යුතුය [C038-M:L3].

sinhala_explanation.heading: සිත දැනගැනීමේ දුෂ්කරතාව: තමන් කපාගත නොහැකි පිහිය (මාර්ගය)
sinhala_explanation.text: සිත ඉතා සියුම්ය; ඇසට නොපෙනේ; සුළඟ, සීතල, උෂ්ණය මෙන් කයට දැනෙන්නක්ද නොවේ; ඉතා ඉක්මනින් ඉපිද බිඳෙන බැවින් පරීක්ෂණයකට හසුකරගත නොහැක [C038-M:L5]. සිතේ සැටි දැනගැනීම ඉතා දුෂ්කර වී ඇත්තේ එය දැනගැනීමේ උපකරණයත් සිතම වීම නිසාය: පිහියෙන් අනිකක් කැපිය හැකි නමුත් පිහියම එයින් කැපිය නොහැක [C038-M:L5]. එබැවින් සිත ගැන නූගත් සාමාන්‍ය ජනයාට චිත්ත වීථියක් ඇති බව පවා නොදැනේ; උගත් අයටද ඇසට පෙනීම වැනි ප්‍රත්‍යක්ෂ දැනුමක් නොව අනුමාන දැනුමක් පමණක් ලැබේ; එහෙත් එය ඉතා ප්‍රයෝජනවත් බැවින් අනුමානයෙන් වුවද දැනගැනීමට උත්සාහ කළ යුතුය [C038-M:L5].

sinhala_explanation.heading: ෂට්ක සය (ප්‍රදීපිකාව)
sinhala_explanation.text: චිත්ත වීථි මනාව දැනගැනීමට ෂට්ක සය දත යුතුය: වස්තු සය, ද්වාර සය, අරමුණු සය, විඤ්ඤාණ සය, වීථි සය, විෂය ප්‍රවෘත්ති සය [C038-P:L33–L35]. වීථියක යම් සිතක් ගැන මෙසේ විමසිය යුතුය: එය චක්බු, සොත, ඝාණ, ජිව්හා, කාය, හදය යන වස්තුවලින් කුමක් ඇසුරු කරයිද; චක්බු ආදි මන දක්වා ද්වාර සයෙන් කුමකටද; රූප ආදි ධම්ම දක්වා අරමුණු සයෙන් කුමක එල්බගනීද; විඤ්ඤාණ සයෙන් කුමක්ද; චක්බුද්වාර ආදි මනොද්වාර දක්වා වීථි සයෙන් කුමකටද; ඒ සිතේ අරමුණ අතිමහන්ත, මහන්ත, පරිත්ත, අතිපරිත්ත, විභූත, අවිභූත යන විෂය ප්‍රවෘත්ති සයෙන් කුමන ආකාරයෙන් වැටහේද [C038-P:L37–L41]. මින් වස්තු, ද්වාර, අරමුණු, විඤ්ඤාණ යන හතර පෙර විස්තර කළ බැවින් දැන් වීථි සය හා විෂය ප්‍රවෘත්ති සය විස්තර කරන බව ප්‍රදීපිකාව කියයි [C038-P:L43].

sinhala_explanation.heading: වීථි දෙවර්ගය: පඤ්චද්වාර සහ මනොද්වාර
sinhala_explanation.text: අරමුණු ඇතුළු කරන ද්වාරය අනුව චිත්ත වීථි දෙවර්ගයකි [C038-P:L47]. චක්බු, සොත, ඝාණ, ජිව්හා, කාය යන ද්වාර පසට වැටුණු අරමුණු එල්බගෙන පවතින සිත් පෙළ පඤ්චද්වාර චිත්ත වීථියයි [C038-P:L49]. මනොද්වාරයට වැටුණු ධම්මාරම්මණයක් එල්බගෙන පවතින සිත් පෙළ මනොද්වාර චිත්ත වීථියයි [C038-P:L51].

key_terms.en: cognitive process: a gapless, ordered series of mind-moments on one object via one door

key_terms.term_si: චිත්ත සන්තතිය / සිත් පෙළ / සිත් වැල
key_terms.en: the continuum or chain of minds
presentation or intensity of the object
very great / great / slight / very slight
key_terms.note: named but not explained in this extract
named but not explained in this extract
Margaya's term for how the process is known

human_interpretation_en.heading: 'I see' is a sequence, not a single act
human_interpretation_en.text: The ordinary feeling is that I simply see, hear, speak or hand something over, all in one go. The source says otherwise: every one of these, even lifting a hand or understanding a single word, is built from a quick, orderly run of separate moments, one after another with no gap between them. What feels like one act is a short procession.

human_interpretation_en.heading: The tool cannot examine itself
human_interpretation_en.text: Margaya is unusually frank. The mind is the hardest thing to study because it is the very thing doing the studying, like a knife that can cut anything except itself. Ordinary people never notice these processes, and even careful students know them only by working backward from what they can observe, never by watching them directly. For a film this is useful honesty: the process itself can never be shown, only its traces in what people do and say.

human_interpretation_en.heading: Six questions you can ask of any moment
human_interpretation_en.text: Pradeepika offers a checklist. For any moment of experience, ask what bodily support it rests on, which channel it came through, what it was about, what kind of knowing it was, which kind of sequence it belonged to, and how strongly the thing presented itself. It is a way of slowing down the description, not the experience.

does_not_transfer: It is not 'slow down and you will see your thoughts arise'. Margaya states that people do not even notice these processes, and that even students know them only by inference.
It is not a 'stream of consciousness' in the literary sense. The source's series is discrete, strictly ordered and tied to one object through one door, not a free associative flow.
It is not 'information processing' in the neuroscience or computing sense, although the analogy is tempting. The source says nothing about brains, and its units are moments of mind, not signals.

The group's framing 'no separate seer behind it' is not stated in these two extracts. Margaya says that acts require a series of minds, and Pradeepika defines the series. Any stronger no-self claim should be sourced from elsewhere, not attributed to C038.

story_seeds.seed: A handloom weaver builds a patterned cloth one pass of the shuttle at a time.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: The rhythm of treadle, shuttle and beater, the pattern appearing line by line, mistakes unpicked, and the weaver's talk about how many passes make a hand-span.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: A whole cloth that looks like 'one thing' is visibly made of many ordered, gapless passes. It is a concrete parallel to an act that feels single but is a series.
story_seeds.risk: Turning the weaver into a metaphor. The film should be about her work and life first.

story_seeds.seed: A court or hospital interpreter moves between Sinhala, Tamil and English for people who depend on being understood.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: An interpreter listening, pausing, rendering, checking and correcting, the listener's face changing as meaning lands, and quiet moments where the interpreter describes how they 'hear' a sentence before translating.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: Margaya lists 'understanding the meaning of another's words' as something no single moment achieves. Interpretation makes that multi-step understanding audible.
story_seeds.setting_type: District court, hospital or government office where interpretation is routine
story_seeds.risk: Legal or medical confidentiality. Filming proceedings may be impossible or inappropriate, so it may need to be limited to training or practice sessions with consent.

story_seeds.seed: A village blacksmith forges and sharpens knives and talks about what a blade can and cannot do.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: The forge, the hammering, quenching, grinding and testing an edge on paper or wood, customers bringing blunt knives, and the smith's hands.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: Margaya's own image is of a knife that can cut everything except itself. The smith's world is full of blades, and the film can hold that thought silently without anyone saying it.
story_seeds.risk: Literal illustration of a simile. The blacksmith's own story must carry the film, or the simile should be dropped.

story_seeds.seed: A three-wheeler driver threads through a busy town junction at rush hour.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: Mirrors, horns, glances, hand signals, sudden braking, and small negotiations with buses and pedestrians. Afterwards the driver can reflect on how much they see without 'thinking'.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: It is an everyday case where countless acts of seeing, hearing and moving happen in quick succession, each, on this account, a whole series of mind-moments.
story_seeds.risk: Generic city B-roll. Filming in traffic has safety implications.

story_seeds.seed: A child in a rural primary school learns to read aloud, sounding out syllables until a word suddenly makes sense.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: The reader's finger under the letters, halting sounds, the teacher's prompts, and the moment a word or sentence comes together.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: Understanding a word is visibly built step by step here, before it becomes fast and invisible in adults.
story_seeds.risk: Filming minors requires school and parental consent. The child's struggle should not be framed as a performance.

cross_source_notes: Pradeepika defines the process through the etymology of 'vīthi' and the object-and-door criterion [C038-P:L29]. Margaya defines it practically, as the chain of minds behind any single act [C038-M:L3].

Margaya includes bodily and verbal acts (speaking, moving limbs, walking, giving, taking) among the things that require a series [C038-M:L3]. The Pradeepika extract speaks only of minds taking an object through a door.
The argument about how hard the mind is to know, the knife simile and the inferential nature of knowledge about the process appear only in Margaya [C038-M:L5].
The six sixes and the division into five-door and mind-door processes appear only in Pradeepika [C038-P:L33–L51]. The Margaya extract does not reach that point.
Both agree that no experience or act is accomplished by one mind-moment.
uncertainties: Both extracts are introductions only. The Margaya file is two paragraphs, and Pradeepika stops right after naming the two kinds of process. The detailed treatment (the six intensities and the process stages) lies in later concepts (C040 onward) and was not read for this digest.
C038-P L29 has probable OCR forms: 'අනෙක' (for අනේක) and 'සඳෙරහි' (for සදෙරහි).
C038-P L37 has missing punctuation in the lists (for example 'ජිව්හා කාය', 'ගන්ධ රස'). The meaning is clear.
The group depth statement ('no separate seer behind it') is not explicitly made in these extracts. It should be sourced from other concepts or checked with an expert before being attributed.
